accessibilityAudit.detailEn: Primary text and buttons are safe.
Compact controls must retain 44pt hit areas.
accessibilityAudit.detailZh: 紧凑模式要保持 44pt 点击区。

accessibilityAudit.detailEn: Clear glass needs scrim and stroke.
accessibilityAudit.detailZh: 清透玻璃需要遮罩和描边。

accessibilityAudit.detailEn: Motion is safe for frequent screens.
Error, locked, and success states are identifiable.
accessibilityAudit.detailZh: 错误、锁定、成功状态可识别。

accessibilityAudit.detailEn: Settings icons, page back, page close, and sheet close have explicit tokens.
accessibilityAudit.detailZh: 设置图标、页面返回、页面关闭和弹窗关闭都有独立 token。

accessibilityAudit.detailEn: Preview uses token colors, not hardcoded white/black.
accessibilityAudit.detailZh: 预览使用 token 色，不依赖硬编码白/黑。

componentRules.background: Global page backgrounds are selected as light/dark pairs. Each official option defines both light-mode and dark-mode gradients in one choice; light backgrounds must remain one step darker than light card surfaces. Large backgrounds use neutral mist / cool gray first, with blue kept as a restrained brand hint instead of a full-screen wash. Custom photo backgrounds use one uploaded image with adaptive light/dark scrims. Power saving reduces motion only and must not override the selected background pair.
componentRules.button: Actions use native SwiftUI Button. Primary actions use the built-in borderedProminent role tinted with goPrimary/adaptivePrimary; keep one primary action per screen and make secondary actions visibly quieter.
componentRules.buttonGrammar: Use native Button roles and built-in styles: borderedProminent for the main command, bordered or automatic for alternate commands, destructive role for danger, and icon-only toolbar buttons only with a localized accessibility label.
componentRules.actionColorDiscipline: goPrimary/adaptivePrimary is the only global click-me color for primary CTAs, confirmations, key navigation, functional icons, focus, and selected system states. Feeding, reminders, danger, success, rewards, and charts may use semantic colors only for domain meaning.
componentRules.solidControlPolicy: High-frequency content buttons, chips, embedded keypads, inputs, list rows, and dense forms use solid fills. This rule does not apply to system navigation chrome or the native interactive lens/thumb of Toggle, Slider, Segmented Control, and DatePicker.
componentRules.controlledGlassPolicy: Use real Liquid Glass only where SwiftUI or UIKit owns the semantic system surface: TabView navigation, top toolbars, system back/close controls, floating system controls, and native control interaction surfaces, plus the explicit member identity-card exception. Sheet, Alert, Menu, and confirmationDialog chrome remains entirely system-managed. Use one glass surface per role, never simulated low-opacity fill and never nested decorative glass.
componentRules.nativeGlassControlPolicy: Toggle delegates to the native SwiftUI switch. Slider, segmented Picker, and DatePicker stay native so Rest, Pressed, Dragging, Selected, and Disabled behavior comes from the system. Figma documents these states and motion; production must not redraw them with custom translucent capsules.
componentRules.calendar: Calendar uses agendaHybrid layout, minimalNumber day cells, dots event markers, and timeRail agenda rows.
componentRules.card: Business surfaces use solidFlat fills by default. Interactive cards, list tiles, achievement cards, dashboards, and quick-action containers use opaque token surfaces such as ohanaCardSurface/ohanaCardSurfaceElevated or solid semantic colors; avoid translucent/frosted card fills except explicit Liquid Glass showcase surfaces. Avoid card nesting.
componentRules.surfaceRhythm: Prefer surface rhythm, spacing, grouping headers, and light hairlines over extra card chrome. Do not add nested cards, decorative borders, or shadows just to create separation.
componentRules.shadowBudget: Ordinary cards, buttons, text, chips, list rows, and modal content do not use decorative shadows. System presentations own their elevation. Reserve custom shadows for toast elevation, critical floating controls, major role/avatar/product visuals, and explicitly allowlisted previews.
componentRules.layoutFitAndSafeArea: Every page must reserve fixed chrome first, then lay out content inside the remaining safe viewport. Meaningful content, hero cards, avatars, charts, buttons, and bottom CTAs must not be clipped by status bars, dynamic island, fixed headers, bottom navigation, safe areas, or host containers. Embedded pages must define explicit top/bottom host insets instead of starting at y=0.
componentRules.visualQualityGate: Before delivery, new or heavily changed UI must pass a fit-and-finish gate: no clipped text or avatars, no duplicate close buttons, no double backgrounds unless each layer is an intentional visible card, no controls hidden behind other layers, no horizontal overflow, and no meaningful content that requires accidental scrolling to discover.
componentRules.layeringAndHitTesting: ZStack layers must have explicit zIndex and hit-testing intent. Decorative backgrounds, masks, glows, scrims, and charts behind controls use allowsHitTesting(false). Foreground buttons, quick actions, and close controls must remain tappable above cards, maps, and motion layers.
componentRules.dynamicContentFit: Layouts must survive long localized German/English/Chinese text, large numbers, missing images, 2.5D full-body avatars, and dense real data. Use fixed aspect ratios, min/max heights, line limits with graceful wrapping, and adaptive scroll only where the scroll is intentional.
componentRules.colorContrastGate: Dark and light mode must be checked together. Glass must remain visibly refractive while preserving readable text; pure dark fills that erase glass depth and low-opacity text over complex backgrounds are not allowed. Semantic colors must come from tokens and cannot conflict with reserved primary colors.
componentRules.chart: Charts use area trend style, quiet axis treatment, and Flow slow line draw for visible data changes.
componentRules.input: Inputs use flat style with clear state emphasis.
componentRules.motion: Motion uses the Ohana Capsule system for custom content only: restrained light elasticity, numericText values, crisp one-shot feedback, staggered custom reveals, and bouncy pop only when reward/status meaning requires it. TabView, NavigationStack, Sheet, Alert, Menu, Form controls, and other semantic system UI keep native motion. Charts are the intentional exception: use Flow slow line draw instead of Capsule pop.
componentRules.pressFeedback: Tap feedback must appear on the finger-first frame through local visual state only: light scale, opacity/brightness, and optional soft haptic. Business writes, SwiftData reads, rewards, reminder sync, and route-heavy work run after the visual handoff.
componentRules.motionContinuity: All visible state changes must transition smoothly with the selected motion token; no hard cuts for controls, toggles, sheets, lists, charts, calendar, or theme changes.
componentRules.motionEnergyBudget: Power saving mode is off by default. Both normal and power-saving modes keep visible interaction motion smooth; power saving only reduces ambient/repeating motion, background refresh, dynamic backgrounds, particles, rainbow flow, and environment glow.
componentRules.zStackMotionScene: Key motion interactions use a stable ZStack scene: keep visual layers mounted, freeze the business snapshot at animation start, and drive transform, mask, opacity, zIndex, and hit testing from one progress value. Do not insert/remove complex views, decode images, scan SwiftData, or run multiple delayed animations during the transition.
componentRules.zStackMotionScope: Required for hero cards, custom spatial reveals, reward reveals, gacha/Oasis rewards, role creation cards, and chart range switching. System controls, menus, sheets, alerts, search, settings, forms, and ordinary lists keep native SwiftUI presentation and motion.
componentRules.spatialHeroCardMotion: Expandable card stacks must have one motion scene own the collapsed frame, expanded frame, inner alignment, padding, avatar source, quick-action bounds, zIndex, hit testing, and ambient floating. Verify the collapsed and expanded end states before tuning springs. Do not fix off-center cards with scattered offsets; first audit CGRect center, inner alignment, leading/trailing padding, overlay bounds, and avatar crop/source.
componentRules.spatialHeroCardHandoff: During collapse, selected layering and frozen visual sources are separate concerns. As the card reaches the collapsed stack, return zIndex/hit testing to the collapsed layer first, keep the frozen card/avatar source for one extra frame, and resume ambient floating only after the live collapsed card has taken over.
componentRules.navigationChrome: Top-level navigation uses native SwiftUI TabView and hierarchical navigation uses NavigationStack. Root tabs render SF Symbols without visible text while retaining localized accessibility labels. The detached home FAB is a native borderedProminent circular Button aligned at the bottom trailing edge; only its placement and custom shortcut menu are app-owned. System tab bars, navigation bars, back buttons, titles, toolbar items, and button states own their glass, interaction, animation, accessibility, and Reduce Transparency behavior.
componentRules.privacy: Locked/private states must show icon + text placeholder and never leak values.
componentRules.icon: Functional icons normally use monochromePrimary: SF Symbol or template-rendered vector glyphs in goPrimary. The approved quick-action glyph component is the only duotone exception: a white primary silhouette plus the active member theme color for semantic detail; pending detail uses 16% opacity and active/completed detail uses full opacity. No skeuomorphic, emoji, or illustration-style glyphs are allowed for navigation, settings rows, lists, or status entries.
componentRules.quickActionIcon: Use the shared 32pt duotone solid geometry set. Keep the white primary layer stationary, animate accent geometry only with one-shot semantic motion, show pending/in-progress/completed states without relying on color alone, and respect Reduce Motion plus AppWorkloadPolicy.
componentRules.settingsIcon: Settings rows use plainGlyph leading icon treatment: no colored tile background, 20-22pt monochrome goPrimary symbol, 44pt hit area.
componentRules.sheet: Present modal content with native SwiftUI sheet(item:) or a typed sheet route. Let the system own detents, drag indicator, safe areas, dismissal, keyboard avoidance, material, and transition; use NavigationStack, Form/List, native toolbar actions, and one borderedProminent CTA inside.
componentRules.sheetPage: Overview, history, quick record, confirmation, management, and complex editor destinations all use native Sheet. Sheet pages use NavigationStack with a real navigation title and native toolbar actions instead of fixed in-page chrome or hand-drawn drag handles.
componentRules.shortPopup: Use Alert or confirmationDialog for short confirmation and destructive decisions, Menu for compact command choices, and Sheet for short record, restock, or lightweight management. Do not implement an in-page modal overlay when one of those semantic presentations fits.
componentRules.shortPopupInterior: Native sheet content uses Form, List, Section, Toggle, Picker, DatePicker, TextField, and built-in Button styles where applicable. Custom cards remain limited to information or visual content without a system equivalent.
componentRules.shortPopupDismissal: Let Sheet, Alert, confirmationDialog, and Menu own dismissal and interactive gestures. Provide an explicit native toolbar cancel/close action only when the flow needs one; do not add outside-tap scrims or custom drag handles.
componentRules.cardUsage: Use card surfaces only for tappable, navigable, or interactive grouped surfaces. Pure information summaries must be unframed inline summaries or metric rows, not card chrome.
componentRules.componentConvergence: Refine one component or variant at a time, store decisions in tokens/rules, and update shared primitives before copying a local visual treatment into multiple feature screens.
componentRules.foodKindColor: Dry food uses global foodDry amber and wet food uses global foodWet rose everywhere. Feeding stock, remaining-food management, and treats use goPrimary; low-stock and error states may use goYellow/goRed locally.
componentRules.primaryColorPolicy: goPrimary resolves to goLime in dark mode and clean goBlue in light mode. These two colors are reserved for global brand/system primary actions, confirmations, functional icons, focus, and selected system states only.
componentRules.memberThemeColor: Pet and human theme colors must use the member palette and must not use goLime, goBlue, or their light/dark primary aliases. Existing reserved member colors are normalized at startup.
componentRules.memberHeroCard: Member identity hero cards (pet, human, plant, and member-creation previews) are the explicit content-layer exception: use one noninteractive nativeRegular glass surface beneath a translucent five-field theme atmosphere, a restrained specular rim, dark top text, white lower text, and no decorative shadow. Reduce Transparency and reduced-effects modes fall back to the opaque five-stop gradient. Photo variants preserve readability with owned scrims.
componentRules.domainColorPolicy: Feeding modes and food kinds use their own semantic colors; feeding stock and treats intentionally use goPrimary. Pet/human theme colors still must not reuse goLime, goBlue, or primary aliases.
componentRules.shortPopupChrome: System presentations own their chrome. Use a native toolbar Button with an SF Symbol when an explicit close action is needed; never draw a replacement sheet shell, drag handle, scrim, or close capsule.

note: Ohana UI guidelines console V4. Preview uses fixture data only and does not mutate app theme.
sceneCoverage: allElements: 全元素总览 / All iOS UI elements in one canvas

navigationChrome: 单色功能图标、设置行左图标、非弹窗返回/关闭、弹窗关闭 / Monochrome functional icons, settings row icons, page back/close, and sheet close
calendar: 日历、日程与提醒设计 / Calendar, agenda, and reminder design
sheetOverlay: 弹窗覆盖层 / Interactive sheet overlay
